description: We are HEXATECHFORCE, a team of six passionate technology enthusiasts participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project, "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map", focuses on helping future astronauts explore Mars safely through interactive maps, hazard detection, safe route planning, and survival resource identification. We are eager to learn, innovate, collaborate, and solve real-world challenges using technology.
summary:
Future human and robotic exploration of Mars requires astronauts and rover operators to navigate unfamiliar terrain while avoiding dangerous cliff scarps and wheel-slippage zones. Developed by Team HexaTechForce, the Martian Terrain Explorer is a functional WebGIS platform built directly on an authentic NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) Context Camera (CTX) GeoTIFF dataset (6.0 meters/pixel) covering Jezero Crater. 

By integrating optical satellite reflectance with calibrated NASA MOLA/HRSC elevation models, the system computes 2D Horn slope gradients, classifies rover traversability hazards into four engineering tiers (Low 0-8°, Caution 8-15°, High >15°, Critical Impassable >25°), and executes an autonomous A* pathfinding algorithm on an 8-connected cost grid. The platform features an aerospace-grade interactive cockpit where users can inspect physical coordinates, evaluate terrain difficulty, and generate lower-cost, obstacle-avoiding traverses with real-time elevation profile comparisons.
details:
WHAT DOES IT DO?

The Martian Terrain Explorer is a full-stack planetary WebGIS and autonomous navigation system focused on the Jezero Crater exploration zone (NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance exploration corridor). Built by Team HexaTechForce, it allows scientists, rover operators, and students to interactively explore high-resolution Martian satellite imagery, inspect genuine physical terrain properties (elevation, slope, albedo), visualize multi-layered hazard masks, and compute physics-based safe traverse routes for autonomous rovers.

HOW DOES IT WORK?

1. Forensic Data Pipeline: The system parses an authentic NASA MRO CTX GeoTIFF (34.6 MB, 5,322 x 5,040 pixels) without altering native georeferencing, projecting it onto the Equirectangular Mars 2000 Sphere IAU (Radius = 3,396,190 m).

2. Topographic & Slope Engine: Fuses CTX imagery with a calibrated NASA MOLA/HRSC Jezero Crater Digital Elevation Model (-2,600m to -1,600m datum). It applies Horn's 2D finite-difference gradient algorithm to calculate exact terrain slopes.

3. Rover Hazard Classification: Categorizes the 965.6 km² study area into four NASA rover mobility safety tiers: Low Hazard (0-8°, Safe), Medium Hazard (8-15°, Caution), High Hazard (>15°, Restricted), and Critical (>25°, Impassable rollover zone).

4. Autonomous A* Pathfinding: Implements an A* algorithm on an 8-connected cost grid utilizing an Octile distance heuristic. Traversal cost grows quadratically with slope steepness, actively steering the path around the steep Western Delta front cliffs while comparing distance, slope, and elevation profiles against straight-line transits.

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES USED

- Backend: Python, Flask 3.1, NumPy, Pillow, Tifffile, python-docx

- Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), Leaflet.js, Canvas API

- Geospatial & Planetary Standards: IAU 2000 Mars Spheroid, Horn 2D Gradient Algorithm, Slippy Map Tiles

- Version Control & Cloud Hosting: Git, GitHub, Render Cloud Platform

CREATIVITY & INTENDED IMPACT

Unlike generic mapping websites, this project honors real planetary physics: it never estimates slope from optical brightness alone, avoids browser memory overload via an optimized web asset pyramid (reducing payload by 97.3%), and delivers an aerospace-grade HUD with zero external paid APIs. It bridges high-level NASA planetary datasets with open-source web technologies for mission planning and STEM education.
